***

## Big idea in one line

An **Interceptor** is Spring MVC middleware around the **handler (controller method)**.  
It is not a servlet Filter: it runs **inside** Spring, knows which controller method was chosen, and has three clear hooks.

```text
Filter(s)
  → DispatcherServlet
      → Interceptor.preHandle
          → Controller
      → Interceptor.postHandle
      → Interceptor.afterCompletion
  ← response
```

***

## Filters vs Interceptors (keep this table)

| | **Filter** | **Interceptor** |
|--|------------|-----------------|
| API | Servlet (`Filter`) | Spring MVC (`HandlerInterceptor`) |
| Knows controller method? | No | Yes (handler argument) |
| Runs if no handler mapped? | Can still run | Tied to MVC handler execution |
| Typical use | Auth gate, encoding, raw logging | Audit handler name, MVC-specific checks, model tweaks |

Use **both** in real apps: Filters for servlet-wide concerns; Interceptors when you need Spring MVC context.

***

## Topic 1 — `HandlerInterceptor` methods

```java
public class LoggingInterceptor implements HandlerInterceptor {

    @Override
    public boolean preHandle(HttpServletRequest request,
                             HttpServletResponse response,
                             Object handler) {
        System.out.println("preHandle: " + request.getRequestURI() + " handler=" + handler);
        return true; // continue to controller
    }

    @Override
    public void postHandle(HttpServletRequest request,
                           HttpServletResponse response,
                           Object handler,
                           ModelAndView modelAndView) {
        System.out.println("postHandle");
    }

    @Override
    public void afterCompletion(HttpServletRequest request,
                                HttpServletResponse response,
                                Object handler,
                                Exception ex) {
        System.out.println("afterCompletion status=" + response.getStatus());
    }
}
```

### Meaning in plain words

| Method | When | Job |
|--------|------|-----|
| `preHandle` | Before controller | Auth check, timing start; return `false` to abort |
| `postHandle` | After controller, before view render | Adjust `ModelAndView` (less common for pure REST) |
| `afterCompletion` | After request fully done (even if errors) | Cleanup, timing end, log final status |

```text
preHandle → returns false → controller SKIPPED
                         → still may call afterCompletion for interceptors that already ran
```

***

## Topic 2 — Register with `WebMvcConfigurer`

```java
@Configuration
public class WebConfig implements WebMvcConfigurer {

    @Override
    public void addInterceptors(InterceptorRegistry registry) {
        registry.addInterceptor(new LoggingInterceptor())
                .addPathPatterns("/api/**")
                .excludePathPatterns("/api/public/**");
    }
}
```

Path patterns give you fine control — similar spirit to filter URL patterns, but in MVC config.

Prefer injecting a `@Component` interceptor bean instead of `new` if it needs other beans:

```java
registry.addInterceptor(loggingInterceptor).addPathPatterns("/**");
```

***

## Topic 3 — Auth-style `preHandle` example

```java
@Override
public boolean preHandle(HttpServletRequest request,
                         HttpServletResponse response,
                         Object handler) throws Exception {
    String key = request.getHeader("X-API-KEY");
    if (!"secret".equals(key)) {
        response.setStatus(HttpServletResponse.SC_UNAUTHORIZED);
        response.setContentType("application/json");
        response.getWriter().write("{\"message\":\"Unauthorized\"}");
        return false;
    }
    return true;
}
```

Same idea as a Filter auth check, but you can also inspect `handler` (e.g. cast to `HandlerMethod` and read annotations on the controller method — useful later with custom annotations).

***

## Topic 4 — Order of multiple interceptors

```text
registry.addInterceptor(A);
registry.addInterceptor(B);

Incoming:  A.preHandle → B.preHandle → Controller
Outgoing:  B.postHandle → A.postHandle
Then:      B.afterCompletion → A.afterCompletion  (reverse for completion too)
```

Registration order matters.

***

## Practice lab (IDE steps)

### Step 1 — Create interceptor

Implement `HandlerInterceptor`; log in all three methods with clear prefixes (`PRE`, `POST`, `AFTER`).

### Step 2 — Register paths

`WebMvcConfigurer` → apply to `/api/**`, exclude one public path.

### Step 3 — Hit endpoints

1. Protected `/api/hello` → see PRE → controller → POST → AFTER.  
2. Excluded public path → interceptor should not run.  
3. Return `false` from `preHandle` without valid header → controller log absent.

### Step 4 — Compare with a Filter

Keep the logging Filter from lecture 19.  
One request should show: **Filter before → Interceptor pre → Controller → Interceptor post/after → Filter after**.

### Step 5 — Read the handler

In `preHandle`, if `handler instanceof HandlerMethod hm`, print `hm.getBeanType().getSimpleName()` and `hm.getMethod().getName()`.

***

## Short map to keep

```text
Filter     = around servlet / DispatcherServlet
Interceptor= around controller handler inside MVC
preHandle  = gate (boolean)
postHandle = after controller (ModelAndView)
afterCompletion = always-ish cleanup
Register via WebMvcConfigurer.addInterceptors
```
